full.description: This image is a gross pathology specimen of the liver. The specimen displays multiple cystic, translucent vesicular lesions scattered throughout the hepatic tissue and within the hilum. These findings are characteristic of hepatic echinococcosis, also known as a hydatid cyst caused by Echinococcus tapeworm infection. The macroscopic appearance shows the characteristic mother and daughter cysts within the affected liver tissue.

random.description: This image is a gross pathology specimen of the liver. The tissue exhibits signs of macronodular cirrhosis, characterized by large, prominent nodules and altered hepatic architecture. The surface also displays cystic-like changes and scarring. The findings are consistent with chronic liver disease, likely secondary to viral hepatitis C.
